correctness.rationale: Every nonsingular order-five feedback table corresponds uniquely to a 16-bit pairing mask. All 65536 masks are tested for a single 32-cycle; independent Eulerian DFS produces identical 2048 masks. For all 120 coordinate-pair changes per valid mask, validity agrees with the alternating conjugate-pair criterion. All-source BFS determines the 368 diametral unordered pairs and exact shortest-path counts. Independently, for each diametral pair, a 7-step 14-coordinate subset DP enumerates precisely the valid disjoint-pair flips and equals its BFS count. The 368-row CSV is replay-checked on actual extracted package files. No reliance on sampling or floating point.

value.rationale: The existing literature studies cross-join transforms as operations that produce and connect universal sequences, and even tabulates degree/one-source reachability. For maximal-distance endpoint pairs, the number of minimum-length transformation histories measures genuine combinatorial flexibility and redundancy not captured by distance alone. The complete natural extremal-domain classification has fourteen distinct large path counts, sharp attained extrema, and a complete per-pair exact dataset. This is substantive finite graph structure, not a one-off arbitrary subparameter or a known table recomputation.
